ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, a uniformly wound solenoid is placed horizontally, and below it a power supply and switch S are connected through wires; in the battery symbol, the long plate is on the left side. Near directly above the exact center of the solenoid hangs a straight wire A. A is represented by a cross inside a circle, indicating that the direction of the current in A is perpendicular to the plane of the paper inward. Reasoning: After switch S is closed, according to the conventional current direction, the current flows out from the positive electrode of the battery, namely the long plate on the left side, enters the solenoid through the left-side wire, and then flows along the solenoid winding toward the right end. Combining the winding direction in the figure, using the right-hand screw rule to judge, the left end of the solenoid is the S pole and the right end is the N pole. Therefore, near directly above the exact center outside the solenoid, the magnetic field direction points from the N pole to the S pole, namely horizontally to the left. The current in wire A is perpendicular to the plane of the paper inward, and the magnetic field is horizontally to the left. According to the left-hand rule or by judging from I×B, the direction of the Ampere force on A is vertically upward.
